clue.text: Gallic charm providing a superior finish

parts.note: Gallic means belonging to France
polish is refinement or elegance of manner, a kind of charm

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's allure gives someone a classy edge.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellac finish gives wooden furniture a high-gloss, top-quality surface.

clue.text: Monarchist dispensing with good, practical person

indicators.note: dispensing with tells us to do without one piece, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a regalist is a supporter of royal power, a monarchist

explanation.surface: A royalist abandons virtue and becomes a hard-headed pragmatist.
explanation.walkthrough: REGALIST is an uncommon word for a champion of the crown; removing G leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deals with things as they actually are is a pragmatic, down-to-earth type.

clue.text: Bedtime drink for a bird

parts.note: night is the time for going to bed
a jar is British slang for a drink, especially a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A nightcap before sleep, offered to a feathered friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedtime drink' looks like one idea (a nightcap) but splits into two pieces; a jar is a pint in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal insect-eating species is known for its churring call.

clue.text: Army chap entertaining

definitions.meaning: a ... is a great multitude, especially an army, as in the heavenly ...
the man receiving guests is the one doing the entertaining

explanation.definitionFit: A biblical multitude of soldiers, and a man who receives and feeds guests at a party.

clue.text: Case dismissed? Quite the reverse — one needs treatment

indicators.note: quite the reverse tells us to swap the order of the two words in the phrase before it

parts.note: in cricket a batter dismissed is out
a case is a patient under a doctor's care

explanation.surface: A court verdict quip: rather than the case being thrown out, someone needs care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' read as PATIENT OUT; 'Quite the reverse' flips it to OUT then PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending hospital for care without staying overnight receives treatment.

clue.text: North of Dundee, it's getting chilly

definitions.meaning: a Dundee is a rich fruit cake from the Scottish city, and the sugary coating sits on its top
turning to ice, freezing over, as in wings on an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: Dundee looks like the Scottish city, but it is the fruit cake named after it; north means the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet topping spread over a cake, and the process of frost forming as things freeze.

clue.text: Throwing energy into possession

indicators.note: into tells us the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: having is owning, being in possession of something
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Putting effort into ownership, perhaps of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to hurl or toss something heavy, so this is tossing.

clue.text: Politician dwelling on confidential article on railway

parts.note: a dwelling is a home
something confidential is secret
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A minister lives above a hush-hush piece about the trains.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just stacks one piece above the next. The Home Secretary is the UK cabinet minister for policing and immigration.
explanation.definitionFit: The British cabinet minister in charge of the Home Office is a senior political figure.

clue.text: A femme fatale is thus — likes toddlers to be around

indicators.note: to be around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A seductress, oddly, is fond of small children and wants them nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's whole definition is a description, 'thus' pointing at the fatal woman; 'to be around' is the anagram signal, read as letters moved around.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman is typically dressed glamorously to make a striking impression.

clue.text: Fruit varieties after the 1st of October

indicators.note: after says the varieties come behind the opening letter
the 1st of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: ranges are assortments or varieties of goods

explanation.surface: Fruit types available after the start of autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruit with a bright peel, the commonest kind of juice fruit.

clue.text: A tune that lacks resonance is nothing

parts.note: a thin sound is weak, lacking depth or resonance
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A feeble, reedy melody amounts to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of their clue order: the description of the sound first, then the tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that vanishes into this has disappeared completely, leaving nothing at all.

clue.text: Be the first to chase an old lover

indicators.note: to chase means following behind, so the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
1st, written with a figure, looks like IST

explanation.surface: Be the one who pursues a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' is written 1ST, and the figure 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is simply to have reality or life.

clue.text: Pub profits from deals

parts.note: a bar is a pub
gains are profits

explanation.surface: A tavern earns money from its transactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Good deals are purchases at low prices, or agreements struck between parties.

clue.text: Debate exchange of hostilities

definitions.meaning: trading hostile remarks, a verbal fight

explanation.definitionFit: A bitter public argument, and a battle fought with insults rather than weapons.

clue.text: Conjunction between Europe and its neighbouring continent could be a mercy

indicators.note: between tells us one piece is placed in the middle of the other two

parts.note: EU is the European Union
Asia is the continent next to Europe
than is a conjunction, used in comparisons

explanation.surface: A grammatical link joining two continents could be merciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjunction' sounds astronomical or geopolitical but is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending life to relieve suffering is often called mercy killing.

clue.text: This monster shot back at soldiers

indicators.note: at places the soldiers beside the turned word
back tells us the word for shot is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a go is a shot, an attempt
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A beast fires back at troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant in fairy tales who eats people is a monster.

clue.text: Some mistake over English flower beds?

parts.note: part means some of something
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Perhaps an error was made concerning English garden borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply stacks the pieces in a down clue. The question mark flags that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal garden with ornamental flower beds laid out in a pattern.

clue.text: Offer a reward to expose unusual…

indicators.note: to expose suggests revealing letters that lie within the words

explanation.surface: Posting a bounty to unmask something out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The trail-off dots lead into the next clue's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found or uncommon.

clue.text: "Get rid of legislation on university"-Tory leader

parts.note: a rule is a regulation or piece of legislation
OU is the Open University, the UK distance-learning university

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leader of Tory is its first letter T

explanation.surface: A protester's slogan demanding that a campus law be scrapped by the Conservative chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university. 'Tory leader' gives the opening letter of Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or eliminate a possibility from consideration.

clue.text: … drinks session catching a traffic controller

indicators.note: catching means the drinks session holds the a inside it

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a bout is a session, as in a drinking bout

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a pub crawl ends up snaring a policeman on point duty.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is a British traffic circle, controlling flow at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular junction regulates the movement of vehicles, so it controls traffic.

clue.text: View no one backs after work at home

indicators.note: after puts the turned piece behind the others

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
in means at home

indicators.note: backs means the words before are read backwards

explanation.surface: Nobody supports a view after a day working from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns NO plus I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief or judgement is a point of view.

clue.text: Address drink problem of air traffic controller

parts.note: to address an audience is to talk
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Discussing the drinking habit of someone in the control tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink problem' looks like one phrase but splits; talking down is guiding a pilot to land by radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiding an aircraft to land by radio instructions is a task facing tower staff.

clue.text: Avoid sharp practice

explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep something, and a cunning scheme or swindle.

clue.text: Mark correct, accepting hothead is none too clever

indicators.note: accepting means the mark holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a tick is the mark showing an answer is right
the head of hot is its first letter H

explanation.surface: A teacher ticks the answer right while letting a firebrand pass, despite dimness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dense or stupid means being none too bright.

clue.text: Mark is almost frightening

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: scary means frightening

explanation.surface: A blemish that is nearly terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting blemish on the skin left by a healed wound.

clue.text: Put in a new requisition for case of rosé or red, possibly

indicators.note: case of picks the outer letters, the shell of the word
possibly signals the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Placing a fresh order for a crate of pink or red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the first and last letters of rosé; 'or' stays as written and 'possibly' rearranges RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To order again is to submit another request for supplies.

clue.text: Friendly face on choir, oddly

indicators.note: on places the face after the picked letters in an across clue
oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: A face appears on the choir in strange fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and amiable in manner.

clue.text: Saw doctors to arrange generous rest

indicators.note: to arrange tells us the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Surgeons plan a lavish break for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw doctors' looks like the past tense of see, but saw is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborists who prune and treat damaged trees are, playfully, doctors who use a saw.
